texts.title: Happy enough?
texts.hook.h1.frame: Your best day… measuring your joy?
texts.hook.h1: Try it: recall your best day… were you measuring your joy?
texts.hook.h2.frame: Chase happiness… and it flies away?
texts.hook.h2: They say happiness is a butterfly: chase it and it flies away… really?
texts.hook.h3.frame: Waiting all year… then: that's it?
texts.hook.h3: I wait all year for this trip… then arrive and say: is that it?
texts.hook.h4: 8,331 people: those who care more about happiness… less happy, or happier?
texts.hook.h5.frame: Happy enough?… Me too. And you?
texts.hook.h5: Nour asks herself: happy enough?… Me too. And you?
texts.s1.n1: This is Nour, on the company trip.
texts.s1.l1: I have to enjoy every minute!
texts.s1.l2: Am I happy enough?… It should be more!
texts.s1.l4: Lovely… but not what I imagined.
texts.s1.a2: And your best day… was there a meter?
texts.s1.n2: Let's play it again… this time, no meter.
texts.s1.l6: Lovely… let's go sit with the others.
texts.book.card: Wanting more good feelings… is itself a bad feeling.
texts.book.l1: The book says: the harder you chase feeling good… the less content you are.
texts.book.l2: Because every « am I happy? »… reminds you of what you lack.
texts.verdict.card: 8,331 Dutch · valuing happiness: better off · as it grew: joy and distress
texts.verdict.nuance: Those who worry about their happiness are worse off… those who seek it with others, more satisfied.
texts.verdict.l2: Sometimes they found happiness-chasers less happy… sometimes happier.
texts.takeaway.l1: Try it like Nour: drop the meter… and sit with people. It may help.
texts.takeaway.orientation: If the distress lasts for weeks and affects your life, talk to a psychologist.
texts.share: Send this to someone who rates every outing.
